sections.heading: What is Ecommerce LTV?: Customer Lifetime Value
paragraphs: LTV (or CLV), Customer Lifetime Value, measures the total profit a customer generates over their entire relationship with your business .

Unlike revenue-focused metrics, this simplified eCommerce LTV formula factors in gross margin to show actual profit contribution. According to Shopify, a good LTV:CAC ratio is 3:1, meaning each customer should generate 3x what you spent to acquire them.

bullets.label: Sets Acquisition Budgets
bullets.text: Knowing LTV tells you how much you can profitably spend to acquire customers

bullets.label: Identifies Valuable Segments
bullets.text: Find which customer groups generate the most long-term profit

bullets.label: Drives Retention Focus
bullets.text: Retained customers buy more often and spend more than new ones

bullets.label: Informs Pricing Strategy
bullets.text: Understand perceived value to optimize product pricing

sections.heading: How to Calculate Ecommerce LTV: The Formula
paragraphs: The simplified eCommerce LTV formula is:
For example, if your AOV is $100 , customers make 6 purchases over their lifetime, with a 40% gross margin , your LTV is $100 × 6 × 0.40 = $100
Each customer generates $100 in gross profit over their lifetime.
sections.formula: LTV = AOV × Purchases per Customer × Gross Margin %

sections.heading: LTV:CAC Ratio Benchmarks
paragraphs: The LTV:CAC ratio shows if your customer acquisition is profitable:
Source: TrueProfit, Shopify (2025). A ratio above 5:1 may indicate under-investment in growth.

bullets.text: Below 2:1: Unprofitable. Spending too much to acquire customers
2:1 to 3:1: Break-even territory. Optimize LTV or reduce CAC
3:1 to 4:1: Ideal balance. Profitable and sustainable growth
Above 5:1: Opportunity to scale. Consider investing more in marketing

sections.note: Source: TrueProfit, Shopify (2025). A ratio above 5:1 may indicate under-investment in growth.

bullets.label: Increase AOV
bullets.text: Use bundles, upsells, and free shipping thresholds

bullets.label: Boost Purchase Frequency
bullets.text: Email marketing, subscriptions, and loyalty programs

bullets.label: Improve Retention
bullets.text: Better onboarding, customer service, and personalization

bullets.label: Optimize Margins
bullets.text: Reduce COGS, negotiate supplier deals, or adjust pricing
